SSD.name: South Sudan
SSD.decision_notes: Lindsey Jones approved the South Sudan pilot for production use on 2026-07-31. The release retains all 19 evidence records and seven pathways from the 12 registered official public sources; source-access, attribution, geographic, and inference limitations remain controlling.

sources.title: Climate, Peace and Security Fact Sheet: South Sudan (2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate, peace, and security conditions synthesized for the 2025 fact sheet.
sources.methodology: SIPRI and partner authors synthesize climate trends, conflict dynamics, institutional context, and policy implications into a country fact sheet with recommended actions.
sources.limitations: The official catalogue states April 2025 without a day, so publication_date preserves month precision; the concise synthesis does not replace review of its underlying sources.

sources.title: Climate Security Risks in South Sudan: An Information Brief (2025)
sources.temporal_coverage: Current climate-security risks and response priorities as assessed in 2025.
sources.methodology: The information brief was jointly developed by UNDP, UNMISS, and the UN Resident Coordinator's Office to synthesize climate-related security risks and strategic interventions for South Sudan.
sources.limitations: This is a short strategic brief rather than a reproducible dataset; its country-level framing can obscure variation among states, livelihood systems, and conflict settings.

sources.title: Joining Forces for a Conflict-Sensitive Flood Response in South Sudan (2025)
geographic_coverage: South Sudan (national and selected flood-affected subnational locations)
sources.temporal_coverage: Lessons from the 2024 flood response and preparedness priorities for the 2025 flood season.
sources.methodology: The article distils a UN Community of Practice discussion and operational examples from UNMISS, OCHA, the UN Country Team, national authorities, and subnational flood taskforces.
sources.limitations: The source is a practice-oriented UN news account, not an independent evaluation; selected operational examples cannot establish how consistently conflict sensitivity was applied nationwide.

sources.title: South Sudan Country Climate and Development Report (2026)
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical climate and development baselines with forward-looking climate and development analysis published in 2026.
sources.methodology: The World Bank country diagnostic integrates climate information with macroeconomic, sectoral, institutional, and development analysis to identify climate-resilient development priorities.
sources.limitations: A national diagnostic may mask subnational differences and depends on model assumptions and uneven underlying data availability; this record does not independently reproduce or verify those inputs.

sources.title: First National Adaptation Plan for Climate Change Republic of South Sudan
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
sources.methodology: The national planning document organizes adaptation around three resilience pillars and nine priority sectors to guide policy and implementation from national to community level.
sources.limitations: The plan records government priorities and intended actions rather than evaluated adaptation outcomes; implementation progress after its 2021-2025 planning horizon requires separate evidence.

sources.title: South Sudan Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of South Sudan and United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate commitments and priorities submitted in 2021, principally oriented to 2030.
sources.methodology: The government submission updates the national greenhouse-gas inventory and sets sectoral mitigation, adaptation, and implementation commitments under the Paris Agreement.
sources.limitations: The date recorded is the UNFCCC submission date, 2021-09-21, not the portal file-publication timestamp; an NDC states commitments and assumptions rather than demonstrating achieved results.

sources.title: South Sudan Flood Damage and Needs Assessment Study (2021)
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
geographic_coverage: Three flood-affected payams in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: Impacts of the June-December 2020 floods, with fieldwork from 2021-08-31 to 2021-10-14.
sources.methodology: IOM field-validated the 2020 flood assessment using two quantitative tools, focus-group discussions, and key-informant interviews, consulting more than 1,131 people across three payams.
sources.limitations: The official page states publication year 2021 without an exact month or day, so publication_date preserves year precision; purposive coverage of three payams is not nationally representative.

sources.title: South Sudan UN Common Country Analysis (CCA)
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office in South Sudan
sources.temporal_coverage: Multisector country context through late 2021, published on the UN portal in 2022.
sources.methodology: The UN country analysis synthesizes political, conflict, humanitarian, socioeconomic, environmental, and institutional evidence to identify constraints to sustainable development.
sources.limitations: The portal publication date, 2022-06-27, is used consistently, while the downloadable document is versioned 2021-12-24; underlying indicators have different reference periods and may have since changed.

sources.title: INFORM South Sudan Country Risk Profile (2021)
sources.temporal_coverage: INFORM 2021 risk profile, including trend displays for 2017-2021.
sources.methodology: INFORM combines standardized indicators of hazard and exposure, vulnerability, and lack of coping capacity into a composite country risk index with peer and trend comparisons.
sources.limitations: The profile identifies version 2021 rather than a dated publication, so publication_date records the stated version year; composite national scores compress indicator uncertainty and subnational disparities.

sources.title: Climate change deepens gender inequality and violence in South Sudan: UNFPA study highlights urgent need for action
sources.organization: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Sudd Institute, and South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics
sources.temporal_coverage: Study findings released in 2025 on current climate-related gender and violence risks.
sources.methodology: The UN story summarizes a vulnerability study conducted by UNFPA with the Sudd Institute and National Bureau of Statistics in three high-exposure locations, with findings validated in a stakeholder workshop.
sources.limitations: This is a summary rather than the full study methodology; purposive selection of three highly exposed locations and condensed reporting limit national generalization.

sources.title: South Sudan Event Tracking Report 73: Flood Displacements (1-31 December 2024)
sources.organization: International Organization for Migration (IOM) Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM)
sources.temporal_coverage: Flood-related displacement events recorded from 2024-12-01 to 2024-12-31.
sources.methodology: IOM DTM enumerators used event tracking to document disaster-related displacement during December 2024 and record affected people's reported priority needs.
sources.limitations: Event tracking is a rapid, period-specific account rather than a complete displacement stock; the 2025-02-10 publication date follows the December 2024 observation period.

sources.title: South Sudan Climatology (ERA5)
sources.organization: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
sources.temporal_coverage: ERA5 climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023.
sources.methodology: The World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal presents ERA5 reanalysis-derived South Sudan climatology for 1991-2020 and historical daily data for 1950-2023 at 0.25-degree resolution.
sources.limitations: ERA5 is model-based reanalysis rather than direct station observation, and national summaries can mask subnational variation. This living page can change and has no fixed publication date; publication_date remains null with basis not-stated.

evidence_records.statement: ERA5 reanalysis presents South Sudan's 1991-2020 climatology and 1950-2023 historical record at daily scale and 0.25-degree resolution; the portal describes a broad historical warming signal while cautioning that reanalysis is model-based and that precipitation trends are harder to distinguish from natural variability.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Use ERA5 as light climate context, retaining its model and precipitation-trend caveats.
institutions: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts

source_refs.locator: named webpage heading 'Climatology (ERA5)', methodology, trends, and 'Data Caveats' sections

evidence_records.uncertainty: ERA5 is model-based; national aggregation masks local variation and supports no social attribution.

evidence_records.statement: The 2025 SIPRI-NUPI fact sheet describes a tropical savannah climate with seasonal White Nile tributary flooding, severe drought and flood exposure, increasing rainy-season precipitation, declining dry-season rainfall, and consecutive floods that no longer reliably recede during the dry season.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen for changing flood persistence and dry-season water stress, not a single uniform hazard trend.

source_refs.locator: page 2, section 'Climate exposure: Trends and projections' and section 'Socioecological vulnerabilities'

evidence_records.uncertainty: Sparse gauges and synthesized datasets limit subnational trend and site-level inference.

evidence_records.statement: The World Bank CCDR key messages project that hotter conditions could reduce sorghum yields by 2050.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen agrifood investments for projected heat-related sorghum yield risk through 2050.

source_refs.locator: official landing-page key-message bullet on hotter conditions and sorghum-yield impacts by 2050

evidence_records.uncertainty: Only official CCDR key messages were accessible; project exposure still needs local assessment.

evidence_records.statement: In flood-affected Rubkona, the SIPRI-NUPI synthesis reports declining livestock holdings and crop farming alongside greater reliance on aid, firewood, and wild foods; it also notes erosion of reciprocal household support and livelihood-related shifts in gender roles, indicating that repeated shocks and conflict can narrow customary coping options.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Assess whether assistance strengthens viable livelihoods and reciprocal coping rather than replacing them.

source_refs.locator: page 2, section 'Livelihood impacts', paragraphs on Rubkona livelihood change and coping mechanisms

evidence_records.uncertainty: Selected qualitative communities are not nationally representative; conflict, markets, and aid also shape coping.

evidence_records.statement: IOM's field validation in three flood-affected payams found damaged or dysfunctional public facilities and reduced road access to health care, markets, and schools; respondents also reported that access constraints prevented aid from reaching some populations and that much facility damage persisted for months.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Map all-season access to facilities and aid routes, including the duration of flood disruption.

source_refs.locator: official webpage numbered results bullet 3, infrastructure and facility-access sub-bullet

evidence_records.uncertainty: Three purposively assessed payams are not nationally representative despite substantial participation.

evidence_records.statement: The same IOM assessment found that floods made farming impossible in many assessed bomas, contributed to livestock loss, changed displacement duration, shifted some communities rapidly between hosting and displacement, and placed additional strain on resources available to communities receiving displaced people.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen livelihood recovery and host-community capacity together because flood displacement can reverse hosting roles.

source_refs.locator: official webpage numbered results bullet 3, livelihood and displacement sub-bullets

evidence_records.uncertainty: Purposive local coverage documents co-occurrence, not a single mechanism producing tension.

evidence_records.statement: The UN Common Country Analysis reports that violence and very poor road infrastructure restrict humanitarian reach, rainy-season conditions make many roads impassable, and conflict and flooding together reduce access to drinking water, health, and nutrition services; it also identifies repeated new and secondary displacement.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Treat violence, seasonal roads, service functionality, and secondary displacement as one access-risk screen.

source_refs.locator: document pages 14-15, paragraphs under humanitarian access, nutrition, and 'Displacement and Population movements'

evidence_records.uncertainty: Mixed reference periods support compound-risk screening, not separate conflict and flood effects.

evidence_records.statement: The 2021 INFORM profile scores South Sudan high across hazard and exposure, vulnerability, and lack of coping capacity, with especially elevated components for uprooted people, governance, physical infrastructure, access to health care, food security, and violent conflict.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Use INFORM to flag compound vulnerability and coping constraints, not to rank individual project sites.

source_refs.locator: page 1, risk-components panel and detailed indicators for vulnerability and lack of coping capacity

evidence_records.uncertainty: The national composite masks subnational variation and supports screening, not causal inference.

evidence_records.statement: A UNFPA-led study summary from Malakal, Kapoeta South, and Rubkona reports that flood, drought, displacement, and economic stress coincide with restricted reproductive-health access, increased gender-based violence, child marriage, and survival-driven exploitation, while flooded facilities and heat events further strain health and education access.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Integrate GBV, child-marriage, reproductive-health, and girls' education safeguards into climate response.
institutions: South Sudan National Bureau of Statistics

source_refs.locator: named webpage headings 'Women and girls at risk: A Climate-Induced Crisis' and 'Call to Action: Gender-Responsive Climate Adaptation'

evidence_records.uncertainty: A summary of three high-exposure locations cannot establish national prevalence.

evidence_records.statement: IOM event tracking recorded 20,109 flood-related displacements during December 2024, concentrated in Twic, Rubkona, and Mayiendit counties, and displaced respondents identified health, shelter, and food as their most pressing needs.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Use current event tracking to size immediate health, shelter, and food needs without treating it as a displacement stock.

source_refs.locator: official webpage summary paragraphs for the 1-31 December 2024 reporting period

evidence_records.uncertainty: One month of reported movements is neither a displacement stock nor long-term assessment.

evidence_records.statement: South Sudan's first National Adaptation Plan states that priority sectors lacked concrete NDC implementation plans and identifies sector vulnerability assessment, capacity building, stronger policy and budget mainstreaming, early warning, and institutional coordination as measures needed to move national commitments toward implementation.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Check whether projects close documented planning, coordination, capacity, budget, and early-warning gaps.

source_refs.locator: document page 72, sections on NDC implementation gaps, five adaptation priorities, and 14 Second NDC sectors

evidence_records.uncertainty: The 2021-2025 NAP diagnoses gaps and plans reforms; subsequent implementation requires verification.

evidence_records.statement: South Sudan's Second NDC sets adaptation priorities for climate-smart agriculture and livestock, water management, health-system resilience, flood and drought early warning, land-use planning, and inclusive participation by local communities, women, youth, civil society, and the private sector.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Align activities with NDC sector priorities while testing participation and implementation capacity locally.
evidence_records.scenario: National adaptation commitments principally oriented to 2030

source_refs.locator: official PDF adaptation section, sector priorities and numbered vulnerable-community actions

evidence_records.uncertainty: NDC commitments and intended measures do not demonstrate consistent implementation or achieved resilience.

evidence_records.statement: The SIPRI-NUPI fact sheet reports that 2024 flooding displaced people across 22 counties and that arrivals in high-ground areas of Unity State added population pressure where food insecurity, displacement, and limited coping capacity were already present; reports linked these pressures with local tensions.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Plan high-ground relocation with host-resource, land-use, food-security, and coexistence safeguards.

source_refs.locator: page 3, section 'Migration and mobility', paragraphs on 2024 flood displacement and Unity State high-ground pressures

evidence_records.uncertainty: Local associations do not establish a deterministic pathway; governance, assistance, and prior disputes matter.

evidence_records.statement: Across the SIPRI-NUPI and UN climate-security syntheses, drought, flooding, and altered seasons are assessed as changing pasture, water, cropland, and pastoral movement conditions; where customary agreements and dispute-resolution mechanisms are weak, these shifts may heighten farmer-herder or cattle-group competition, while local dialogues have produced shared livelihood-protection rules.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Support negotiated mobility and resource-sharing rules before changing water, pasture, or cropland access.

source_refs.locator: pages 2-3, sections 'Livelihood impacts' and 'Migration and mobility', including UNMISS dialogue outcomes
official information brief, context section and strategic-interventions bullet on livelihoods, mobility, early warning, and peacebuilding

evidence_records.uncertainty: Climate and mobility are rarely sole drivers; weapons, elite incentives, disease, and disputes matter.

evidence_records.statement: SIPRI-NUPI documents cases where floodwater compounded landmine risk and prevented people from following evacuation advice, while prolonged inundation and violent land-grabbing constrained safe return; it also notes that some flood conditions produced temporary cooperation rather than violence.
evidence_records.compact_statement: Assess mines, contested tenure, land-grabbing, and negotiated access before evacuation, return, or relocation.

source_refs.locator: page 4, section 'Armed actors and security', paragraphs on Pigi evacuation, land-grabbing, and temporary cooperation

evidence_records.uncertainty: Documented examples are not nationally prevalent; mines, armed actors, land claims, and cooperation alter outcomes.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Screen whether conflict and institutional weakness are constraining climate adaptation capacity.
evidence_records.statement: The SIPRI-NUPI fact sheet and UN Common Country Analysis assess that conflict, political instability, weak rule of law and public institutions, limited infrastructure, and low trust reduce the capacity of households and institutions to prepare for, adapt to, and recover from climate-related shocks.

source_refs.locator: page 2, section 'Climate change and peace and security', paragraphs on governance, trust, infrastructure, and adaptive capacity
pages 14-15, section on humanitarian access, public services, infrastructure, and conflict- and flood-related disruption

evidence_records.uncertainty: The synthesis cannot isolate institutional or conflict effects from poverty, displacement, and infrastructure deficits.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Climate-security pathways can pass through livelihoods, mobility, recruitment, and elite exploitation
evidence_records.statement: The Climate Security Mechanism brief identifies livelihood disruption, displacement and mobility, recruitment incentives, and elite exploitation of climate-related pressures as possible pathways linking climate stress and insecurity, and recommends conflict-sensitive peacebuilding, early warning, policy integration, and coordination as responses.

source_refs.locator: sections on climate-security pathways and strategic interventions, including livelihood disruption, mobility, recruitment, elite exploitation, early warning, and coordination

evidence_records.uncertainty: Possible pathways are not quantitative attribution and remain conditional on local conflict and political economy.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Conflict-sensitive flood response combined high-ground preparation with community dialogue
evidence_records.statement: The Climate Security Mechanism reports that the 2024 conflict-sensitive flood response plan identified 243 high-ground locations and supported more than 30 awareness campaigns and dialogues, including a Yirol dialogue involving host communities, displaced people, and cattle keepers.

source_refs.locator: heading 'United for Resilience', paragraphs on the 2024 conflict-sensitive response plan, 243 high grounds, more than 30 campaigns and dialogues, and Yirol

evidence_records.uncertainty: Reported activities lack independent outcome evaluation and evidence of consistent implementation.

evidence_records.compact_statement: Localized forecasting and dialogue face language, finance, supply, and trust constraints
evidence_records.statement: The Climate Security Mechanism describes localized forecasting, community knowledge, youth engagement, and dialogue as resilience capacities, while identifying warning communication, language, financing, and supply gaps that can limit timely preparedness in fragile settings.

source_refs.locator: headings 'From Crisis to Capacity' and 'Forecasting Fragility', paragraphs on warning and language gaps, financing and supplies, forecasts, local knowledge, youth, and localized planning

evidence_records.uncertainty: Program experience does not compare the effectiveness of different resilience or conflict interventions.

pathways.documented_impact: Flood displacement, prolonged stays on high ground, livelihood loss, and pressure on receiving communities
pathways.fcv_mediator: Scarce dry land and services, repeated displacement, weak infrastructure, and strained host-community resources
pathways.possible_consequence: Localized disputes or tensions may become more likely where displaced and host communities must share limited land, water, services, and livelihood resources
alternative_explanations: Conflict, poverty, service deficits, and pre-existing land disputes can independently drive displacement and host-community tension.
pathways.uncertainty: Localized pressure is documented; tension is neither universal nor primarily attributable to flooding.
resilience_factors: services that benefit host and displaced communities
pathways.compact_statement: Repeated flooding may increase localized host-displaced tension when displacement concentrates people on scarce high ground with limited services and livelihood resources.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood, drought, and rainfall variability affecting pasture, water, and seasonal access
pathways.documented_impact: Altered pastoral mobility, livelihood disruption, and greater interaction between cattle keepers and farming communities
pathways.fcv_mediator: Weakened customary route agreements, weapons availability, cattle-raiding dynamics, and uneven local dispute-resolution capacity
pathways.possible_consequence: Farmer-herder disputes and cattle-related violence may intensify where changed mobility is not coordinated through trusted agreements
alternative_explanations: Political mobilization, cattle-raiding economies, weapons availability, and unresolved land claims can drive violence without a climate shock.
pathways.uncertainty: Mobility can support adaptation; tension depends on weak coordination and cannot be generalized.
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related livelihood and mobility changes may raise farmer-herder tension when customary route agreements and dispute-resolution arrangements are weak.

pathways.documented_impact: Damaged or impassable roads and facilities, interrupted public services, and reduced humanitarian reach
pathways.fcv_mediator: Violence, insecurity, limited infrastructure redundancy, and uneven public and humanitarian presence
pathways.possible_consequence: Unequal or delayed access to health, food, education, water, and protection may deepen exclusion and grievances in already fragile locations
alternative_explanations: Chronic underinvestment, poor maintenance, administrative exclusion, and active conflict can restrict services even without flooding.
pathways.uncertainty: Joint access constraints are documented; grievance or violence effects are unmeasured.
pathways.compact_statement: Flooded infrastructure and insecurity can jointly restrict service and humanitarian access, with possible implications for exclusion and grievance.

pathways.climate_pressure: Repeated flood and drought shocks affecting crops, livestock, wild foods, and market access
pathways.documented_impact: Food insecurity, livelihood loss, reduced reciprocal support, and reliance on aid or environmentally damaging coping options
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict-related market disruption, displacement, poverty, gender inequality, and limited livelihood alternatives
pathways.possible_consequence: Households may adopt harmful coping strategies or face heightened recruitment, exploitation, or protection risks when food and livelihood options contract
alternative_explanations: Macroeconomic crisis, armed conflict, displacement, market failure, and aid shortfalls may independently produce food insecurity and harmful coping.
pathways.uncertainty: Food and livelihood stress is documented; harmful coping and recruitment prevalence is unquantified.
pathways.compact_statement: Repeated shocks may increase harmful coping and protection risks when conflict, poverty, displacement, and weak markets leave households few livelihood alternatives.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flooding, heat, and drought affecting shelter, livelihoods, schools, and health services
pathways.documented_impact: Displacement, unsafe shelter, economic hardship, school closure, and reduced health and sexual and reproductive health access
pathways.fcv_mediator: Gender inequality, conflict-related protection gaps, service disruption, and limited safe livelihood options
pathways.possible_consequence: Women and girls may face heightened gender-based violence, intimate-partner violence, exploitation, child marriage, and health risks
alternative_explanations: Conflict, displacement, economic crisis, and entrenched gender inequality independently create severe protection and health risks.
pathways.uncertainty: Protection risks are underreported; climate, conflict, poverty, and inequality effects remain inseparable.
resilience_factors: continuity of health and protection services
pathways.compact_statement: Climate-related displacement and service disruption may heighten gendered protection and health risks where conflict and inequality already restrict safety and services.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flood, drought, heat, and climate variability requiring coordinated adaptation and preparedness
pathways.documented_impact: High exposure and vulnerability create sustained demand for early warning, public investment, sector planning, and local response capacity
pathways.fcv_mediator: Conflict, political instability, weak rule of law and institutions, limited infrastructure, low trust, and policy and budget implementation gaps
pathways.possible_consequence: Adaptation investments and warnings may be delayed, uneven, or less effective, leaving households and institutions more vulnerable to subsequent shocks
alternative_explanations: Low income, sparse infrastructure, technical constraints, and donor fragmentation may impede adaptation independently of conflict and institutional fragility.
pathways.uncertainty: Institutional constraints are documented; individual effects and implementation consistency are not compared.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict and weak institutions can constrain adaptation capacity when instability, low trust, infrastructure deficits, and implementation gaps disrupt planning and delivery.

pathways.climate_pressure: Flooding and persistent inundation that require evacuation, return, or relocation
pathways.documented_impact: Flood-affected people may need to cross, temporarily occupy, or return to land outside their usual settlements
pathways.fcv_mediator: Landmine contamination, armed-actor presence, land grabbing, contested tenure, and weak land governance
pathways.possible_consequence: Safe evacuation, return, and relocation options may narrow, while land disputes or protection risks may increase
alternative_explanations: People may remain or move for livelihood, family, service-access, or security reasons unrelated to flooding.
pathways.uncertainty: Examples are not nationally prevalent and include cooperation; local mine, land, and security arrangements determine outcomes.
pathways.compact_statement: Conflict legacies and contested land can restrict climate-related evacuation, return, or relocation where routes and destinations are unsafe or disputed.
